Mayoral Mayhem

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Why are so many Mayors across the country involved in fatal motor accidents?

Unique Selling Point:
An interview with the father of the young man killed in the accident involving the former Mayor of Johannesburg, the late Jollidee Matongo.
An interview with the driver of the truck that was struck by the former Mayor of Ekhurhuleni, Mzwandile Masina.

Summary:
We take a look at 5 recent motorcar accidents involving municipal mayors. These accidents have claimed the lives of 9 people, including 3 mayors. In most cases the mayors were driving themselves after curfew. In one case the mayor was being driven by the SAPS VIP Protection Unit. We ask does this position of privilege lead to disregard for the rules and recklessness on the road? Can we rely on the authorities to give accurate accident reports and pursue justice in the case of negligence?



Further information:
20 August 2020 - Ekurhuleni
A large goods truck driving down the N12 West highway near Alberton was struck from behind by a black BMW 540i driven at high speed. The BMW was driven by Mayor Mzwandile Masina, breaking curfew in a city-owned (VIP blue light) car he had used without permission. The Mayor was shouting at the truck driver, who alleges the Mayor was drunk. Mayor Masina was removed from the scene by his wife before police investigations had finished and no witness statement was taken from him. The EMPD and the Mayor’s VIP Protection entourage also arrived at the scene. The accident report says drunken driving was not suspected, nor was it tested for. Amabhungane suspects the accident was hushed up. No further investigations have occurred and the Mayor’s spokesperson explained that he broke curfew because he was attending to a medical emergency concerning a close family relative in Katlehong.

28 August 2021 – Nelson Mandela Bay (Gqeberha)
Mayor Nqaba Bhanga is seriously injured when his Mercedes Benz collides with an Audi at an intersection in Algoa Park at 23h30 (breaking curfew). It is the Mayor’s 44th birthday and he is driving his personal vehicle. Two other people, 44-year-old Nonzwakazi Maho and her friend, the 39-year-old driver Sindile Ronald Sicolo are killed.

3 October 2021 – Naledi (Vryburg & Stella)
Mayor Neo Schalk was killed in a head-on collision on the N14 outside Vryburg in the early hours of the morning (breaking curfew). The driver of the other vehicle was also killed.

2 January 2022 – Emalahleni (Witbank & Middelburg)
Mayor Linah Malatjie and her husband Esau were killed in a head-on collision on the R554 between Gemsbokspruit and Verena, Mpumalanga at 21h30. The driver of the other car was killed on impact.

18 September 2021 – Johannesburg
Mayor Jolidee Matongo was killed when his BMW X5 collided with a small bakkie and a pedestrian on the Golden Highway near Lenasia. The driver of the bakkie, 23-year-old Sagel Singh and an unidentified pedestrian were also killed. The Mayor was in his official vehicle, driven by members of the VIP Protection Unit. Both these members survived.
JMPD source told Carte Blanche that their original report found the BMW X5 struck the pedestrian first and then collided with thebakkie. The Mayor’s office demanded they change their original report to say the opposite. When they refused they brought in CSI from Pretoria.
Sagel’s father, Satish Singh, was given an accident report by the JMPD that aligns with CSI’s findings. He is disputing the facts and feels there is a cover-up. There are no witness statements included in the report, and no data printouts from Tracker or the BMW X5’s Crash Data Recorder. When he went to Lenasia SAPS to get the eye-witness statement in the docket, he was sent packing.
Singh has written to the new DA Mayor and IPID asking for an investigation.

Singh also submitted the JMPD report to an independent expert Konrad Lotter from Du Metier. Lotter disputes some of the findings but says one cannot prove negligence of either driver.

Possible trip to Port Elizabeth for presenter & producer if former Mayor Bhanga and family of the deceased agree to an interview.
Possible extra shoot day in PE if Nqaba Bhanga and family of deceased agree to an interview.

Script:


MAYORAL MAYHEM

V/O: In South Africa the number of road deaths increases every year – and some of those involved are VIPs.

Text: Linah Malatjie
Mayor of Emalahleni
2 January 2022

On the 2nd of January this year – the Mayor of Emalahleni
Linah Malatjie and her husband Esau were killed in a head-on collision in Mpumalanga. The driver of the other car was killed on impact.

Text: Neo Schalk
Mayor of Naledi
3 October 2021

On the 3rd of October last year Naledi Mayor Neo Schalk, was killed in a head-on collision in the North West. The accident happened at 3.00am during curfew and also killed the other driver.

Text: Mzwandile Masina
Mayor of Ekurhuleni
20 August 2020

V/O: On the 20th of August 2020 long distance truck driver Sipho Luthuli was driving a pantechnicon truck and trailer to Kimberley. It was just after midnight when he was overtaken by a car on the N12 in Alberton.
Sipho:
00:02:15 When it drove in front of me it was swerving, I could see that the driver was not alright. I flashed my lights, and then he changed lanes and went to the 2nd lane. When we were supposed to curve he didn’t on his lane. He went straight into the trailer at the back.

V/O: The other car was a black BMW belonging to the EMPD’s VIP Protection Unit. The driver was the Mayor of Ekurhuleni, Mzwandile Masina.

Bongani: He said I changed lanes . And then I said to him if I had changed lanes this man would have gone under the trailer.

Bongani: Then what did they say when you told them that?

Sipho: When he got out of the car I saw that he was drunk.

Bongani: How could you see that he’d been drinking?

Sipho: I could see, I could see.

V/O: The police spoke to me and took my statement. When they finished they went to speak to him and that's when the police took him away because they could see that he was drunk.

V/O: This allegation was recorded in Luthuli’s sworn statement that night, but the Mayor left the scene without giving a sworn statement.

Thepa: The only time statements are taken and registered is when a case docket must be registered for the purpose of injuries which might have been sustained at the scene of the accident, or where there’s fatalities.

V/O: Chief Supertindent Kelebogile Thepa is the EMPD Spokesperson.

Bongani: There’s been an allegation that Masina may have been driving under the influence on the night in question?

Thepa: We can confirm that no alcohol was suspected – the use thereof – nor was it also tested.

Link: We know that South Africans are notoriously bad drivers, but what explains this spate of car accidents involving Mayors? Is it just tragic coincidence or is that Mayors feel the rules don’t apply to them, and they won’t be held accountable?

V/O: But not only was Mayor Masina breaking curfew, he wasn’t permitted to drive the VIP Protection vehicle.

Bongani: Was Masina authorized to drive that vehicle that night?

Thepa: No, with the exception of the fact that an emergency had occurred.

Bongani: What emergency?

Thepa: A family emergency, which had resulted in the death of one of the family members.

Bongani: Do we have proof that there was indeed this emergency?

Thepa: Yes, we do.

Link: Mzwandile Masina has lost his mayorship as well as his VIP Protection detail. He refused an interview with Carte Blanche saying he wasn’t drunk on the night of the accident, and in fact there was no accident - it was just a minor collision.

Text: Nqaba Bhanga
Mayor of Nelson Mandela Bay
28 August 2021

V/O: On the 28th of August last year the Mayor of Nelson Mandela Bay Nqaba Bhanga was celebrating his birthday. At 11.30pm that night he was seriously injured when his Mercedes Benz collided with an Audi at this intersection in Algoa Park. Two people were killed: the 39-year-old driver Sindile Sicolo, and 44-year-old businesswoman Nonzwakazi Maho.

Amanda: Nzwaki was the first-born, she was everyone’s mother in the house.

V/O: Family member “Amanda” has asked us to conceal her identity for fear of being targeted.
00:03:49
Amanda: I was woken up by the police and the neighbours.

Bongani: What did they tell you?

Amanda: They first asked about a car that was registered in the house – a grey Audi. And then I confirmed the car is my sister’s car. And then they said there were two people that passed away – a female and a male.

Link: On the night of the accident South Africa still had a 10:00pm curfew. The Mayor’s explanation for breaking curfew was that he was attending to a medical emergency. However it’s been reported he was not breathalyzed, and his blood alcohol level was not tested.

V/O: Bhanga underwent surgery and two weeks later tweeted a video showing his recuperation in hospital. He also offered his condolences to the bereaved families and said his family would pay them a visit.

Bongani: Did anyone in his family come and see you?

Amanda: His sister and a pastor. They said he was in critical condition in hospital, but as soon as he’s out he’s gonna come. We’ve been waiting.

V/O: Within two months Bhanga was back on the campaign trail for the Democratic Alliance, but it seems the accident may have dented his popularity.

Link: Nqaba Bhanga lost his mayorship in the recent municipal elections and is now the leader of the DA opposition in the province. He refused an interview with Carte Blanche saying he hasn’t been charged with anything.

V/O: Instead he referred us to this video statement he tweeted in September.
00:01:36
Bhanga: I’m so heartbroken that this accident took two lives. I have met the police today in relation to the accident and I’ve submitted a statement and the accident is under investigation.

Link: It’s been 6 months since Sandile and Nzwaki were killed in the collision with the mayor, but the Accident Report has still not been finalized. Our request for an interview with the Eastern Cape police was ignored.

Text: Jolidee Matongo
Mayor of Johannesburg
18 September 2021

V/O: In September last year the Mayor of Johannesburg Jolidee Matongo was returning home from campaigning in Soweto with President Ramaphosa. He was a passenger in the back seat of his VIP Protection BMW. At 7.30pm a pedestrian ran across the Golden Highway and was hit by a Nissan bakkie. The driver of the bakkie swerved into the oncoming BMW. Both the pedestrian and the Mayor were killed on impact.
00:02:12
Satish: My eldest son called me and he said to me Dad, Sagel is involved in an accident and he’s looking fine, but he’s trapped in the vehicle.

V/O: Satish Singh’s 22-year-old son Sagel, was the driver of the Nissan bakkie. He had to be cut of the vehicle and was conscious when taken to hospital, but later died from his injuries.

Satish: You know lucky are those that die before their children. This is an absolute heart-breaking event that has taken place in our family.

V/O: But the subsequent investigation and Accident Report by the JMPD has raised Singh’s suspicions of a cover-up.
00:07:53
Satish: The investigating officer did visit our family on several occasions. On the first occasion he said to us that it was the Mayor’s vehicle that had actually struck the pedestrian. He made his second visit and he mentioned to my son that has been approached and he’s being pressured to change his story. And on his third visit he said to us it was actually my son who knocked a pedestrian.

V/O: We showed the Accident Report to an independent expert, forensic engineer Konrad Lotter. He disagreed with a few findings but came to the same conclusion as the JMPD.

Konrad: This sketch is very accurate in relation to indicating the location of the vehicles on the road and the angles at impact and the probable rotation that would have occurred after that.

Bongani: What happened, how did we end up there?

00:16:42
Konrad: There was probably a pedestrian that was running across the road. The driver of the Nissan reacted to the pedestrian. But that is an emergency situation. There's absolutely nothing you can do. The pedestrian was thrown in the direction that the vehicle was moving, but he also carried his own speed.
So the driver of the BMW would have noticed this vehicle swerving and he swerved slightly to his left. And approximately at the same time the pedestrian flying through the air struck the BMW on its roof, the impact between the two vehicles occurred.

Bongani: Do we have any records from the BMW data, crash data?

Konrad: It is not part of the report, but it should actually be.

V/O: But the JMPD investigator raised some red flags himself.

00:09:36 One of the first things he highlighted to us was that the pedestrian was lying on the floor between both vehicles, and next to him was an unbroken Sky vodka bottle. And the investigating officer expressed to us that the bottle was placed there.

Konrad: The probabilities of a bottle being 100% intact right next to the pedestrian is extremely strange.

Satish: He said my son carried the pedestrian 34 metres on his bonnet before he collided with the Mayor’s car.

Konrad: For me that is unlikely.

Satish: In his report he states that the pedestrian penetrated my son’s windscreen, and therefore there was a lot of blood found on the passenger airbag of the NP 200. The windscreen is lying on the bonnet after it was removed by emergency services when they used the jaws of life to extract my son. And the windscreen was never penetrated. So this begs the question: how did the pedestrian’s blood end up on the airbag?

Link: The JMPD won’t speak to us about their Accident Report claiming that the matter is under judicial consideration, and therefore prohibited from public discussion elsewhere – basically sub judice.

V/O: We asked lawyer Pooja Dela if the rule applies in this case.

Pooja: I can’t tell you how many times we’ve heard that from police officials, state officials, politicians who simply throw up their hands and say sub judice, the matter is before the court, I can’t comment. The rule does not provide a blanket prohibition to denude public officials from the duties of accountability and transparency. They are well within their rights to refuse to comment, but it’s incorrect as a matter of law to say I’m prohibited because of the sub judice rule.

V/O: Satish Singh has now asked the Mayor of Johannesburg, Dr Mpho Phalatse for an independent investigation.
00:02:17
Phalatse: He needs to write a formal complaint to the JMPD because the person who wrote the statement was a JMPD officer. The JMPD has an IPID equivalent which is internal affairs, and there is capacity to look into the matter. But what I also know is that the matter has been handed over to SAPS for further investigation. The driver of the vehicle on the night is now part of my protection detail as well, and he says no, there would be absolutely no reason to cover anything up.


Satish: I’m not out to get people to lose their jobs. All I want is the truth. I want to close this final chapter with the truth.

V/O: And it’s these lingering doubts that the families need to be resolved before they can find closure.

The Mayor’s explanation for breaking curfew was that he was attending to a medical emergency. However it’s been reported he was not breathalyzed, and his blood alcohol level was not tested. V/O: Bhanga underwent surgery and two weeks later tweeted a video showing his recuperation in hospital. He also offered his condolences to the bereaved families and said his family would pay them a visit. Bongani: Did anyone in his family come and see you? Amanda: His sister and a pastor. They said he was in critical condition in hospital, but as soon as he’s out he’s gonna come. We’ve been waiting. V/O: Within two months Bhanga was back on the campaign trail for the Democratic Alliance, but it seems the accident may have dented his popularity. Link: Nqaba Bhanga lost his mayorship in the recent municipal elections and is now the leader of the DA opposition in the province. He refused an interview with Carte Blanche saying he hasn’t been charged with anything. V/O: Instead he referred us to this video statement he tweeted in September. 00:01:36 Bhanga: I’m so heartbroken that this accident took two lives. I have met the police today in relation to the accident and I’ve submitted a statement and the accident is under investigation. Link: It’s been 6 months since Sandile and Nzwaki were killed in the collision with the mayor, but the Accident Report has still not been finalized. Our request for an interview with the Eastern Cape police was ignored. Text: Jolidee Matongo Mayor of Johannesburg 18 September 2021 V/O: In September last year the Mayor of Johannesburg Jolidee Matongo was returning home from campaigning in Soweto with President Ramaphosa. He was a passenger in the back seat of his VIP Protection BMW. At 7.30pm a pedestrian ran across the Golden Highway and was hit by a Nissan bakkie. The driver of the bakkie swerved into the oncoming BMW. Both the pedestrian and the Mayor were killed on impact. 00:02:12 Satish: My eldest son called me and he said to me Dad, Sagel is involved in an accident and he’s looking fine, but he’s trapped in the vehicle. V/O: Satish Singh’s 22-year-old son Sagel, was the driver of the Nissan bakkie. He had to be cut of the vehicle and was conscious when taken to hospital, but later died from his injuries. Satish: You know lucky are those that die before their children. This is an absolute heart-breaking event that has taken place in our family. V/O: But the subsequent investigation and Accident Report by the JMPD has raised Singh’s suspicions of a cover-up. 00:07:53 Satish: The investigating officer did visit our family on several occasions. On the first occasion he said to us that it was the Mayor’s vehicle that had actually struck the pedestrian. He made his second visit and he mentioned to my son that has been approached and he’s being pressured to change his story. And on his third visit he said to us it was actually my son who knocked a pedestrian. V/O: We showed the Accident Report to an independent expert, forensic engineer Konrad Lotter. He disagreed with a few findings but came to the same conclusion as the JMPD. Konrad: This sketch is very accurate in relation to indicating the location of the vehicles on the road and the angles at impact and the probable rotation that would have occurred after that. Bongani: What happened, how did we end up there? 00:16:42 Konrad: There was probably a pedestrian that was running across the road. The driver of the Nissan reacted to the pedestrian. But that is an emergency situation. There's absolutely nothing you can do. The pedestrian was thrown in the direction that the vehicle was moving, but he also carried his own speed. So the driver of the BMW would have noticed this vehicle swerving and he swerved slightly to his left. And approximately at the same time the pedestrian flying through the air struck the BMW on its roof, the impact between the two vehicles occurred. Bongani: Do we have any records from the BMW data, crash data? Konrad: It is not part of the report, but it should actually be. V/O: But the JMPD investigator raised some red flags himself. 00:09:36 One of the first things he highlighted to us was that the pedestrian was lying on the floor between both vehicles, and next to him was an unbroken Sky vodka bottle. And the investigating officer expressed to us that the bottle was placed there. Konrad: The probabilities of a bottle being 100% intact right next to the pedestrian is extremely strange. Satish: He said my son carried the pedestrian 34 metres on his bonnet before he collided with the Mayor’s car. Konrad: For me that is unlikely. Satish: In his report he states that the pedestrian penetrated my son’s windscreen, and therefore there was a lot of blood found on the passenger airbag of the NP 200. The windscreen is lying on the bonnet after it was removed by emergency services when they used the jaws of life to extract my son. And the windscreen was never penetrated. So this begs the question: how did the pedestrian’s blood end up on the airbag? Link: The JMPD won’t speak to us about their Accident Report claiming that the matter is under judicial consideration, and therefore prohibited from public discussion elsewhere – basically sub judice. V/O: We asked lawyer Pooja Dela if the rule applies in this case. Pooja: I can’t tell you how many times we’ve heard that from police officials, state officials, politicians who simply throw up their hands and say sub judice, the matter is before the court, I can’t comment. The rule does not provide a blanket prohibition to denude public officials from the duties of accountability and transparency. They are well within their rights to refuse to comment, but it’s incorrect as a matter of law to say I’m prohibited because of the sub judice rule. V/O: Satish Singh has now asked the Mayor of Johannesburg, Dr Mpho Phalatse for an independent investigation. 00:02:17 Phalatse: He needs to write a formal complaint to the JMPD because the person who wrote the statement was a JMPD officer. The JMPD has an IPID equivalent which is internal affairs, and there is capacity to look into the matter. But what I also know is that the matter has been handed over to SAPS for further investigation. The driver of the vehicle on the night is now part of my protection detail as well, and he says no, there would be absolutely no reason to cover anything up. Satish: I’m not out to get people to lose their jobs. All I want is the truth. I want to close this final chapter with the truth. V/O: And it’s these lingering doubts that the families need to be resolved before they can find closure. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Why are so many Mayors across the country involved in fatal motor accidents?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: An interview with the father of the young man killed in the accident involving the former Mayor of Johannesburg, the late Jollidee Matongo. An interview with the driver of the truck that was struck by the former Mayor of Ekhurhuleni, Mzwandile Masina.
metadata.Summary: We take a look at 5 recent motorcar accidents involving municipal mayors. These accidents have claimed the lives of 9 people, including 3 mayors. In most cases the mayors were driving themselves after curfew. In one case the mayor was being driven by the SAPS VIP Protection Unit. We ask does this position of privilege lead to disregard for the rules and recklessness on the road? Can we rely on the authorities to give accurate accident reports and pursue justice in the case of negligence?
metadata.Further information: 20 August 2020 - Ekurhuleni A large goods truck driving down the N12 West highway near Alberton was struck from behind by a black BMW 540i driven at high speed. The BMW was driven by Mayor Mzwandile Masina, breaking curfew in a city-owned (VIP blue light) car he had used without permission. The Mayor was shouting at the truck driver, who alleges the Mayor was drunk. Mayor Masina was removed from the scene by his wife before police investigations had finished and no witness statement was taken from him. The EMPD and the Mayor’s VIP Protection entourage also arrived at the scene. The accident report says drunken driving was not suspected, nor was it tested for. Amabhungane suspects the accident was hushed up. No further investigations have occurred and the Mayor’s spokesperson explained that he broke curfew because he was attending to a medical emergency concerning a close family relative in Katlehong. 28 August 2021 – Nelson Mandela Bay (Gqeberha) Mayor Nqaba Bhanga is seriously injured when his Mercedes Benz collides with an Audi at an intersection in Algoa Park at 23h30 (breaking curfew). It is the Mayor’s 44th birthday and he is driving his personal vehicle. Two other people, 44-year-old Nonzwakazi Maho and her friend, the 39-year-old driver Sindile Ronald Sicolo are killed. 3 October 2021 – Naledi (Vryburg & Stella) Mayor Neo Schalk was killed in a head-on collision on the N14 outside Vryburg in the early hours of the morning (breaking curfew). The driver of the other vehicle was also killed. 2 January 2022 – Emalahleni (Witbank & Middelburg) Mayor Linah Malatjie and her husband Esau were killed in a head-on collision on the R554 between Gemsbokspruit and Verena, Mpumalanga at 21h30. The driver of the other car was killed on impact. 18 September 2021 – Johannesburg Mayor Jolidee Matongo was killed when his BMW X5 collided with a small bakkie and a pedestrian on the Golden Highway near Lenasia. The driver of the bakkie, 23-year-old Sagel Singh and an unidentified pedestrian were also killed. The Mayor was in his official vehicle, driven by members of the VIP Protection Unit. Both these members survived. JMPD source told Carte Blanche that their original report found the BMW X5 struck the pedestrian first and then collided with thebakkie. The Mayor’s office demanded they change their original report to say the opposite. When they refused they brought in CSI from Pretoria. Sagel’s father, Satish Singh, was given an accident report by the JMPD that aligns with CSI’s findings. He is disputing the facts and feels there is a cover-up. There are no witness statements included in the report, and no data printouts from Tracker or the BMW X5’s Crash Data Recorder. When he went to Lenasia SAPS to get the eye-witness statement in the docket, he was sent packing. Singh has written to the new DA Mayor and IPID asking for an investigation. Singh also submitted the JMPD report to an independent expert Konrad Lotter from Du Metier. Lotter disputes some of the findings but says one cannot prove negligence of either driver.
